key_insight: Conventional amplitude encoding makes nonzero real rescalings indistinguishable to any downstream quantum circuit, but a fixed nonlinear feature map removes this ambiguity.
engineering_relevance: The proposed encoding improves input distinguishability without adding trainable parameters while retaining logarithmic qubit scaling.
method: Establish an architecture-independent expressivity restriction caused by normalization-induced scale invariance.
Derive a condition for preprocessing to remove the ambiguity, showing that nonlinearity alone is insufficient.
Introduce a fixed nonlinear feature map that distinguishes all real inputs after amplitude encoding.
evidence_signal: On three canonical classification benchmarks and one nonlinear synthetic dataset, the proposed encoding reportedly improves accuracy by 21–44% over conventional amplitude and angle encoding; a classical neural network is also evaluated.
watch_item: Logarithmic qubit scaling does not establish efficient state preparation, and the abstract does not quantify loading costs or hardware-noise robustness.
paper_title: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
